headline: CRML CLEARS GREENLAND'S LAST HURDLE: TANBREEZ MINING PLAN APPROVED THROUGH 2050 — 28.7-BILLION-TONNE HEAVY RARE EARTH COMPLEX IS OFFICIALLY OPEN
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (Nasdaq: CRML) disclosed October 5 that Greenland's Minister of Mineral Resources formally signed the Tanbreez Mine's mining plan on September 29, authorising extraction of 19 rare and critical elements — including dysprosium, terbium, yttrium, neodymium-praseodymium, zirconium, hafnium, tantalum, and niobium — through the year 2050. The Tanbreez carbonatite complex in southeastern Greenland is one of the world's largest known heavy rare earth deposits; the mining plan approval removes the principal regulatory overhang, though activity-specific operating permits are still required before extraction commences. CRML shares rose 10.8% on the news, with the project sitting outside China's dominance of global rare earth supply and inside a NATO ally jurisdiction that qualifies for DFARS-compliant sourcing.

headline: SILVER POWERS +2.1% TO $61.71 AS YTD-HIGH DOLLAR STALLS GOLD BELOW $4,200 — DEUTSCHE BANK WARNS 6-YEAR DEFICIT COULD FLIP TO 2027 SURPLUS
snippet: Silver jumped 2.1% to $61.71 per ounce on October 5 — significantly outperforming gold, which was pinned between $4,138 and $4,179 by a U.S. dollar index at its strongest level since April 2025 — as industrial demand held firm ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. The outperformance came despite contrarian research from Deutsche Bank circulated the same day warning that silver's sixth consecutive annual supply deficit could flip to a structural surplus as early as 2027 if AI-linked industrial demand softens, creating a divergence between near-term price momentum and longer-term structural uncertainty heading into the FOMC decision.

headline: HAMMER METALS $80.7M COPPER TAKEOVER HEADS TO SHAREHOLDER VOTE NOV. 9 AFTER FEDERAL COURT CLEARS SCHEME MEETING
snippet: Hammer Metals (ASX: HMX) shareholders will vote November 9 on Austral Resources Australia's proposed acquisition — 1.2903 new Austral shares per Hammer share, implying A$80.7 million — after Australia's Federal Court approved the scheme meeting following early polling showing approximately 95% support. The transaction consolidates Queensland copper operations in the Mt Isa district, with Hammer's West Australian gold assets to be divested ahead of close; the Hammer board unanimously recommends the scheme. Final court approval remains a condition precedent, making the November 9 vote the critical next milestone.

headline: ASEAN+3 ECONOMISTS RAISE RED FLAG: AI DEMAND BUBBLE REVERSAL COULD DEMOLISH COPPER AND LITHIUM PRICE FORECASTS
snippet: The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office published an October 5 analysis warning that AI-linked manufacturing and data-centre demand — a key underpinning of copper and lithium consumption projections since 2024 — is vulnerable to a sharp correction that would rapidly undermine the demand thesis behind current metal prices. The report specifically identifies Latin American producers, where Chile's copper output has already fallen to a 15-year low, as having minimal production buffer to absorb a simultaneous demand-side shock; the scenario is characterised as a tail risk that mining equity valuations are not currently pricing.

headline: ASX JUNIOR GOLD BOOM: EXPLORERS SPEND RECORD A$566M IN Q2 AS CASH RESERVES HIT ALL-TIME A$12 BILLION HIGH
snippet: Australian gold explorers committed a record A$566 million to exploration in the June 2026 quarter — up 24% quarter-on-quarter — while total cash held by ASX-listed explorers hit an all-time high of A$12 billion, according to October 5 analysis drawing on Geoscience Australia data. Gold exploration alone rose 47.8% year-on-year to A$1.93 billion, the strongest pace since 2012, driven by gold near A$6,500/oz. The analysis cautions that Q4 2026 drill results will either validate current market enthusiasm or trigger a selective rotation out of explorers that fail to convert the record spending into discovery.

headline: MCLAREN MINERALS MML OCTOBER TITANIUM UPDATE: LATEST 74-HOLE BATCH AVERAGES 5.44% HEAVY MINERALS — TREND IMPROVING ON PRIOR PROGRAMME
snippet: McLaren Minerals (ASX: MML) released results from the latest batch of its 2026 drilling campaign at the McLaren Titanium Project in Western Australia on October 6, with 74 reverse circulation holes averaging 5.44% heavy minerals from surface — an improvement on the 4.96% HM average across the prior 179-hole programme. The project features shallow, dune-hosted ilmenite mineralisation adjacent to the established WA titanium processing corridor; the improving grade trend across successive batches supports a maiden resource estimate targeted later in 2026, positioning the project for growing non-China TiO₂ feedstock demand.

headline: FORTUNA METALS FUN DRILLS 50KM KAMPINI RUTILE TARGET NEXT TO SOVEREIGN'S KASIYA — LARGEST UNTESTED TITANIUM ENDOWMENT IN MALAWI
snippet: Fortuna Metals (ASX: FUN) commenced Phase 1 drilling at the Kampini Rutile Project in Malawi on October 6, testing a 50-kilometre target corridor immediately adjacent to Sovereign Metals' Kasiya deposit — the world's largest rutile reserve. An aircore programme on a 200m by 200m grid evaluates surface anomalies identified by soil sampling and geophysics; historical holes returned up to 7 metres at 2.19% TiO₂, and Phase 1 results will drive resource modelling for a potential Phase 2 expansion. Rutile demand is structurally supported by the push for non-China titanium feedstock for aerospace sponge and high-grade pigment manufacturers.

headline: AUSTRALIA'S CHIEF ECONOMIST LIFTS COPPER PRICE DECK FOR 2026-2028 — ASX PRODUCERS SEE FORWARD EARNINGS UPGRADES
snippet: Australia's Office of the Chief Economist published its October 2026 Resources and Energy Quarterly with upward copper price revisions across 2026–2028, reflecting persistent supply shortfalls at Chilean and Indonesian operations alongside structural demand growth from power infrastructure and AI data centres. The upgrade is the second consecutive AOCE copper revision and triggers forward earnings increases for ASX producers including Sandfire Resources and Aeris Resources, while validating exploration capital being deployed by junior copper developers in tier-1 jurisdictions outside Chile's operational risk zone.
